concerns.text: Task T001 is tagged `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but it creates the project directory tree, which is a prerequisite for many subsequent tasks. Running it in parallel with any consumer task would cause failures. The `[P]` tag is therefore unsafe.

Task T011a creates `code/config.py` with constants used throughout the pipeline (e.g., BATCH_SIZE, DRIFT_THRESHOLD). It is marked `[P]` but later tasks depend on these constants, so it cannot be safely run in parallel. Remove the `[P]` tag.

Task T005 is marked `[P]` yet it produces raw data files that are required by downstream tasks (T006, T007, etc.). It also assumes the directory structure created by T001/T002. Therefore it is not parallel‑safe.
Task T006 depends on the output of T005 (taxonomy examples) and on constants from T011a. Marking it `[P]` is incorrect because it cannot execute before its producers.
Task T007 consumes centroids from T006 and raw logs from T005. Its `[P]` tag is unsafe; it must run after both producers.
Task T008 reads `drift_scores.parquet` produced by T007. The `[P]` tag suggests it could run in parallel, which would break the data dependency.
Task T009 creates annotation batches from `full_range_sample.json` generated by T008. It cannot be parallel‑safe.
Task T010 ingests human annotations based on the batches from T009. Its `[P]` tag is invalid.
Task T011 performs statistical validation using the gold‑standard from T010 and drift scores from earlier phases. It must not be parallel‑safe.
Task T012 runs the Flan‑T5 baseline and relies on constants from T011a and the sampled logs from T008/T009. The `[P]` tag is inappropriate.
Task T013 compares metrics from T011 and T012; it cannot execute before both producers, so `[P]` is unsafe.
Task T014 generates the final report using outputs from T013 and CI logs. It must run after those tasks; `[P]` is misleading.
Task T015 creates reproducibility audit documentation that references the final report from T014. It cannot be parallel‑safe.
